name: Bittensor
rootCause: On July 2, Bittensor's blockchain enlightenment was rudely interrupted by a $8 million hack, due to a compromised PyPi Package Manager. As validators meditated on their nodes, an attacker silently drained their wallets faster than you can say "om."

descriptions.text: On July 2, Bittensor's blockchain enlightenment was rudely interrupted by a $8 million hack, due to a compromised PyPi Package Manager. As validators meditated on their nodes, an attacker silently drained their wallets faster than you can say "om."

On July 2, 2024, the decentralized AI project Bittensor was attacked, resulting in some Bittensor wallet users being compromised. The hackers stole approximately 32,000 TAO tokens, valued at around $8 million. On-chain investigator ZachXBT suggested that the attack may have been due to a private key leak. However, Bittensor later clarified that the affected users were actually compromised because a malicious Bittensor package had been uploaded to the Python PyPi package manager.

On July 2, 2024, Bittensor's supply-chain infrastructure was compromised by a malicious PyPI package, leading to the theft of approximately $8 million in TAO tokens from user wallets. The attack exfiltrated unencrypted private keys from those running wallet operations, prompting an immediate chain halt. No public attacker transaction or malicious code artifacts are available for review. A trojanized Python package (masquerading as Bittensor v6.12.2) was published on PyPI.
